claim: Let \(Q_3\) be the graph on \(\{0,1\}^3\) with edges joining vertices that differ in one coordinate, and let \(\Delta_k(Q_3)\) be its ordinary \(k\)-cut complex. Then \(\Delta_4(Q_3)\simeq\bigvee^{3}S^2\), while \(\Delta_5(Q_3)\) is simplicially the disjoint union of the boundaries of the tetrahedra on the even- and odd-parity vertex classes, hence \(\Delta_5(Q_3)\cong S^2\sqcup S^2\). Moreover, the filtration inclusion \(\Delta_5(Q_3)\hookrightarrow\Delta_4(Q_3)\) is null-homotopic.
integrity: All finite subset enumeration and boundary calculations are exhaustive and replayable from the included verifier. The homotopy conclusion additionally uses standard Hurewicz and homological Whitehead theorems.
scientific_limitations: Exact only for the three-cube and cut levels 4 and 5; no general higher-dimensional hypercube statement is claimed. A residual originality risk remains from unindexed small-graph computations.
title: Upper cut-complex transition of the three-cube
